transcript:
User: Oh you remind me of my nephew — he's in prison again, third time, anyway my chihuahua needs surgery which costs more than my car, what was I saying? Oh! My neighbor's tree fell on my fence in 2019...
Agent: Oh wow—sounds like you’ve had a lot going on. What made you call Dialux today?
User: Well, I was thinking about how my aunt's roof caved in during a storm, and thought of calling you.
Agent: Got it—“how my aunt's roof caved in during a storm,” that’s scary. What’s the main thing you’re worried about right now—missing emergency calls, getting inspections booked fast, or something else?
User: Oh, definitely missing calls! Speaking of which, my son just called about dinner plans, and I lost track.
Agent: Makes sense—when things feel urgent it’s easy to lose track. When a call comes in and you miss it, what usually happens next—do they leave a voicemail, text you, or just call someone else?
User: Oh, I usually get a voicemail! My cousin leaves the longest ones, can you believe she still talks about prom?
Agent: Yeah, long voicemails can really slow you down. Roughly how many calls a week hit voicemail?
User: Oh, about as many times as my cat demands treats! He's so picky, just like my voicemail inbox.
Agent: Mhm—so it’s pretty frequent. What kind of business is this for, where those missed calls are coming in?
User: Oh, it's like when my garden gets overrun with weeds—I just can't keep up. You know?
Agent: Yeah, totally—things pile up fast. Are you running something like landscaping or tree service, or is it a different kind of business?
User: Oh, that reminds me of when my hibiscus bloomed unexpectedly! My brother thought I should start a plant nursery.
Agent: Got it. What kind of business do you actually run today?
User: Oh, speaking of businesses, my sister tried opening a bakery but her oven broke. Such a mess!
Agent: Sounds chaotic. What’s your business called—or if that’s easier, what do you do for customers day to day?
User: Oh, my days are like juggling flaming torches! Ever felt like your to-do list grows overnight?
Agent: I hear you. What do you do for work—are you booking jobs, taking appointments, or selling something in person?
User: Oh, work! My cousin’s wedding was a full-time job planning. Everything’s a whirlwind, like when my dog chased the mailman!
Agent: Right—life gets loud. Are the missed calls coming from customers trying to book something with you, or are they more personal calls?
User: Oh, a mix! Like when my sister calls about her kids while I'm juggling doctor's appointments and pet drama.
Agent: Got it—a mix of personal and customers. For the customer calls you miss, what do you want to happen instead—get them booked right away, or at least capture the details so you can call back fast?
User: Oh, that reminds me of my cousin's wedding! Such chaos with details. I'd love to call back fast, though!
Agent: Got it—so the big win is capturing the details so you can call back fast. When those customer calls go to voicemail and you can’t get back quickly, do you feel like you’re losing bookings to someone else?
User: Oh, it can feel like when my brother misses his train! But then, there's always another one, right?
Agent: I hear you—sometimes it feels like there’s always another one. When someone calls and you don’t get back to them the same day, do they usually try you again, or do they disappear?
User: Oh, they usually pop up again! Like my mom when I forget to call back about her garden.
Agent: Got it—so a lot of them do try again. What’s the one type of call you really can’t afford to miss?
User: Oh, the doctor’s office! Missing that is like when my puppy ran off with my keys—chaos!
Agent: Got it—missing calls at the doctor’s office can turn into real chaos fast. When you miss those calls, is it usually new patients trying to book, or existing patients with something urgent?
User: Oh, it's usually existing ones in a hurry, like when my mom misplaces her glasses and blames the dog!
Agent: Got it—existing patients in a hurry is a big deal. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation to show what missed calls could be costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead! Though it reminds me of my sister's math struggles in school, bless her heart.
Agent: Perfect—super quick. Ballpark, how many calls a week hit voicemail? 10, 20, 30?
User: Oh, it's like my mom's shopping trips: unpredictable. Could be 10, could be 30, just depends on the week!
Agent: Got it—let’s take a middle number so the math’s fair: would you say 20 missed calls a week is about right?
User: Oh, 20 sounds close! Like trying to guess how many cookies my aunt sneaks during her visits.
Agent: Okay—20 a week. Of those missed calls, what percent do you think would’ve actually booked an appointment if you’d answered—maybe 30%, 50%?
User: Oh, like my dad's fishing trips—50% might have reeled in, but you never know!
Agent: Got it—50%. And what’s an average appointment worth for you, roughly, in dollars?
User: Oh, probably like when my cousin splurges on concert tickets, around that ballpark. Speaking of, have you been to any concerts lately?
Agent: I haven’t—wish I had time lately. Roughly what number should we use for an average appointment value: $100, $150, $250, or something else?
User: Oh, about $150 seems right! Like the cost of my weekly groceries when I splurge on organic produce.
Agent: Got it—at 20 missed calls a week, 50% booking rate, and $150 each, that’s about **$1,500 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$6,400 over a month**. Does that feel about right to you?
User: Oh, math never was my strong suit! Sounds like my brother's budgeting—always surprising! But hey, life’s unpredictable, right?
Agent: Totally—life’s unpredictable, which is exactly why catching those urgent patient calls matters. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—I'll show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Oh, choosing is tough! Like when my niece can't pick ice cream. My schedule's just as messy right now.
Agent: Totally get it—sounds like one of those weeks. If you had to pick, is **later today** more realistic, or **tomorrow**?
User: Oh, today’s like a whirlwind with my dog’s vet visit. Tomorrow might be calmer, but who knows!
Agent: Got it—tomorrow sounds better. What time tomorrow usually works for you: morning, afternoon, or evening?
User: Oh, mornings are chaos with my cat’s antics, afternoons blend into errands. Evenings might work if dinner isn’t a crisis.
Agent: Evenings make sense. What’s your first name?
User: Oh, names remind me of when my niece was born! Family is big, so we were debating for weeks!
Agent: Haha—families can make a name decision feel like a whole project. What’s your first name?
User: Oh, names! Like when my sister's baby was born. Such drama over it! Speaking of, did I tell you about...
Agent: I hear you—real quick so I can get this set up: what’s your first name?
User: Oh, names can be tricky! Like when my cousin debated baby names for months. Can we chat about something else?
Agent: Got it—happy to switch gears. Do you want to keep going on the missed-calls issue, or talk about something completely different?
User: Oh, missed calls! Like when my brother forgets his phone everywhere. But did I mention my dog's new tricks?
Agent: Got it—missed calls are the main thing. When a call comes in and you can’t pick up, do they usually leave a voicemail, or do they just call the next office?
